context: Early-return from handle_existing_database when catalog == 'postgres' so the decision is made solely post-ATTACH by _resolve_postgres_catalog_reuse, and correct the false docstring claim. Consider whether reuse should require the benchmark's EXPECTED tables rather than 'any user table present' - other adapters check expected tables - but that is a wider change; keep this fix to the postgres path.
description: handle_existing_database() decides reuse from self.metadata_path.exists(). For catalog=postgres that path is meaningless but still computed to a default, so a leftover .ducklake file from an earlier duckdb-catalog run at the same benchmark/scale sets database_was_reused=True. The runner then skips schema creation and data loading, and validation fails against an empty PostgreSQL catalog. Reproduced at TPC-H SF=1 on 2026-07-30: 'Empty tables detected: region, nation, supplier, part, partsupp, customer, orders...' with a genuinely fresh PG catalog (ducklake_table empty). PR #1358 added post-ATTACH reuse resolution for postgres (_resolve_postgres_catalog_reuse) but did not stop the pre-connection check firing, and its docstring wrongly claims a postgres catalog never has a local metadata file. This blocks any real postgres-catalog benchmark run.

preserves.behavior: duckdb/sqlite catalogs keep deciding reuse from metadata_path exactly as today
